messages.author: af46f37e5a5fa00d
messages.subject: Bug in titan_cluster.sh?
parts:
When running the TITANRunner pipeline, one of the scripts called *titan_cluster*.sh failed, with this error:

> data <- loadAlleleCounts(tc_het_file, symmetric=sym)
titan: Loading data /extscratch/morinlab/shared/rmccloskey/colorectal_exome/14_titan/01-1-010-1_R0027/titan/intermediate_R0027/01-1-010-1_01-1-010-1_010-BF_010-BF_tumour_counts_hetpsns.txt
Error in read.table(file = file, header = header, sep = sep, quote = quote,  : 
  duplicate 'row.names' are not allowed
Calls: loadAlleleCounts -> read.delim -> read.table
Execution halted

The reason seems to be that the tumor_counts_hetpsns.txt looks like this:

1 848671 G 0 X 0
1 861630 G 5 X 2 4
1 869303 C 0 X 1 2
1 878331 C 24 X 36 43
1 878809 C 8 X 3 11
1 883035 A 0 X 0
1 895792 G 3 X 2 5
1 908823 G 24 X 17 46
1 909073 C 10 X 11 15
1 909309 T 10 X 13 16
...

Notice the "extra" seventh column and the fact that the first row doesn't have it, so R thinks the file only has 6 data columns and is treating the first column as row names.

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Bug in titan_cluster.sh?
parts:
Hi Rosemary,

This seems to be a bug in the "count.py" script that prepares input files for TitanCNA.  The quickest fix that you can apply now is to simply cut out the last column.  This column is not actually used by TitanCNA and was a legacy feature from past versions. 

We will address this in the upcoming release of the pipeline.

Thanks for bringing this up.

Best,
Gavin
